mainTopic: Why רבי יוחנן needed to list a courtyard, תרומה and a sale as things that fix produce for מעשר only once its work is finished, and three lessons learned from a ברייתא about buying figs from an עם הארץ.
overview: Just before this amud, רבי יוחנן taught that a courtyard, separating תרומה, and a sale make produce 'fixed' for מעשר only once its work is finished. The גמרא explains that 'courtyard' rejects רבי יעקב and 'תרומה' rejects רבי אליעזר. For 'sale' it brings a teaching about buying figs from an עם הארץ, and draws three lessons from it. It then shows that the sale rule rejects the תנא קמא of a משנה about swapping fruit. With that, פרק המביא ends and a new פרק begins. The new משנה allows lowering produce through a skylight on יום טוב to save it from rain, and allows covering things or placing a vessel under a leak. The גמרא lists five accepted versions of the משנה's first word, all meaning 'to make fall down,' with a source for each. Finally it asks how much produce may be lowered. It answers 'four or five baskets,' then challenges that answer from both directions, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The courtyard item rejects רבי יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן said a courtyard fixes produce for מעשר only when its work is finished. He said this to reject the view of רבי יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The courtyard rule was said in order to exclude the view of רבי יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן included 'courtyard' in his list: it pushes aside the opinion of רבי יעקב. The source for רבי יעקב's view comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item in רבי יוחנן's list needs a reason for being there. Here the reason is to rule against a תנא who held that a courtyard fixes produce even before its work is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: Courtyard. Bringing produce into one's courtyard can make it 'fixed' for מעשר.
To exclude; to rule out a certain opinion.

phrases.english: Courtyard: this comes to exclude the view of Rabbi Ya'akov.

steps.triggerLanguage: חצר — לאפוקי מדרבי יעקב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of why each item in רבי יוחנן's list was needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The courtyard item rejects רבי יעקב, who holds that a courtyard fixes produce even before its work is finished.

steps.title: Source: figs carried through the courtyard to be dried
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that figs carried through a courtyard to be dried may be eaten casually without מעשר. A ברייתא adds that רבי יעקב requires מעשר and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה exempts.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Someone carries figs through his courtyard to dry them. His children and household may eat from them casually and are exempt from מעשר. A ברייתא teaches about this: רבי יעקב obligates, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רבי יעקב holds a courtyard fixes produce even when its work is not finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The figs are still on their way to being dried, so their work is not finished. The משנה, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, say the courtyard does not fix them, so a snack (עראי) is allowed. רבי יעקב requires מעשר, which means he holds the courtyard fixes them anyway. That is the view רבי יוחנן is ruling out.

keyTerms.meaning: To lay figs out to dry.
Casual eating, a snack, as opposed to a set meal.
Tithe that must be separated from produce.
Obligates / exempts.

phrases.english: As we learned: one who carries figs through his courtyard to lay them out to dry,

phrases.aramaic: בָּנָיו וּבְנֵי בֵּיתוֹ אוֹכְלִין מֵהֶן עֲרַאי,
phrases.english: his children and household members may eat from them casually,
and they are exempt from tithes.
And it was taught about it: Rabbi Ya'akov obligates,
and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda exempts.

steps.triggerLanguage: דתנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יעקב's view mentioned in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יעקב holds a courtyard fixes produce even before its work is finished.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about figs carried through a courtyard to be dried, together with the ברייתא recording the disagreement.

steps.title: The תרומה item rejects רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן said separating תרומה fixes produce only when its work is finished. He said this to reject the view of רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תרומה rule was said in order to exclude the view of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא explains the next item on the list, תרומה. It was said to push aside רבי אליעזר. The source comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the courtyard item. A specific item is needed to rule against a specific תנא who held it fixes produce even before the work is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן. Separating it can fix produce for מעשר.

phrases.english: Teruma: this comes to exclude the view of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: תרומה — לאפוקי מדרבי אליעזר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in רבי יוחנן's list, using the same pattern as step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תרומה item rejects רבי אליעזר, who holds that separating תרומה fixes produce even before its work is finished.

steps.title: Source: תרומה separated before the work was finished
steps.stepSummary: A משנה records a disagreement about fruit that had תרומה separated before its work was finished. רבי אליעזר forbids snacking on it, and the חכמים permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Fruit from which תרומה was separated before its work was finished: רבי אליעזר forbids eating from it casually, and the חכמים permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that shows רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר forbids even a snack, so he holds that separating תרומה fixes the fruit even though its work is unfinished. The חכמים permit a snack, so for them it is not fixed. רבי יוחנן rules like the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Their work was finished; the produce is fully processed.
Forbids / permit.
The Sages; the majority opinion.

phrases.english: As we learned: fruits from which he separated teruma
before their work was finished,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹסֵר לֶאֱכוֹל מֵהֶן עֲרַאי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer forbids eating from them casually,
and the Sages permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דתנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי אליעזר's view mentioned in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר holds separating תרומה fixes unfinished produce.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about fruit with תרומה separated before its work was finished.

steps.title: Source for the sale item: figs bought from an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: For the sale item, the גמרא brings a teaching about someone who buys figs from an עם הארץ in a place where people usually press figs into cakes. The buyer may snack on them and later tithes them as דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sale: as we learned: One who buys figs from an עם הארץ, in a place where most people press them, may eat from them casually, and he tithes them as דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: For the last item, a sale, the גמרא first brings a source that matches רבי יוחנן's rule, without yet naming an opinion it is ruling out. Step 7 names that opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that place the figs are not finished until they are pressed. Even though they were bought, the buyer may still snack on them. This shows the sale did not fix them. Once they need tithing, he separates only דמאי, the 'doubtful' tithe.

keyTerms.meaning: A purchase or sale.
An unlearned person, not trusted to have separated מעשר properly.
Press, as in pressing figs into cakes.
Produce of doubtful tithe status, bought from an עם הארץ, which is tithed out of doubt.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a sale never fixes produce. The point is only that a sale does not fix produce whose work is still unfinished.

phrases.english: Sale: as we learned:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: one who buys figs from an am ha'aretz,
in a place where most people press them,
may eat from them casually,
and he tithes them as demai.

steps.triggerLanguage: מקח — כדתנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the last item in רבי יוחנן's list. This time the גמרא brings a supporting source instead of naming an opinion to rule out.
steps.raayaObject: That a sale does not fix produce whose work is not finished.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching about buying figs from an עם הארץ in a place where people press figs.

steps.title: Three lessons from the figs teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws three rules from the figs teaching. First, a sale fixes only finished produce. Second, most עמי הארץ do separate מעשר. Third, we tithe דמאי from an עם הארץ even for produce whose work was not finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this. Learn that a sale fixes produce only when its work is finished. Learn that most עמי הארץ do tithe. And learn that we separate דמאי from produce of עמי הארץ even when its work was not finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up by pulling three separate lessons out of the figs teaching from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lesson one: he may snack after buying, so the sale did not fix the unfinished figs. Lesson two: he separates only דמאי and not a full certain tithe, which shows most עמי הארץ do tithe. Lesson three: even though the figs were bought before their work was finished, the דמאי obligation still applies to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; a conclusion drawn from a source.
Three.
Fixes; makes produce obligated in מעשר.
They separate tithes.

steps.whatToRemember: A sale fixes produce for מעשר only once its work is finished. Most עמי הארץ do tithe, so their produce is only דמאי. That דמאי tithing applies even to produce bought before its work was finished.
steps.whyThisMatters: These lessons explain why produce from an עם הארץ is treated as doubtful (דמאי) and not as certainly untithed, which is a basic idea in the laws of מעשר.

phrases.english: Learn from it three things.
Learn from it: a sale does not fix produce
except for something whose work is finished,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: רוֹב עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מְעַשְּׂרִין הֵן,
phrases.english: and learn from it: most amei ha'aretz do tithe,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מְעַשְּׂרִין דְּמַאי מֵעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: and learn from it: we tithe demai from produce of amei ha'aretz
even for something whose work was not finished.

steps.triggerLanguage: שמע מינה תלת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws conclusions from the figs teaching quoted in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A sale fixes only finished produce; most עמי הארץ tithe; and דמאי applies even to produce bought before its work was finished.

steps.title: The rule rejects the first opinion in the fruit-exchange משנה
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a sale fixes only finished produce is meant to reject the תנא קמא, who says an exchange always creates a מעשר obligation. רבי יהודה says it depends on what each person plans to do with the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This excludes what we learned in a משנה: If someone swaps fruit with his friend, whether both plan to eat it, both plan to dry it, or one plans to eat and one plans to dry, they are obligated in מעשר. רבי יהודה says: the one who plans to eat it is obligated, and the one who plans to dry it is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us whose opinion the first rule from step 6 is arguing against. It is the תנא קמא of a משנה about two people swapping fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא holds that a swap, which counts as a sale, makes the fruit חייב במעשר even if its work is not finished. רבי יהודה holds that a swap makes the fruit חייב only for the person whose work is finished, meaning the one who will eat it now. Our rule, a sale fixes only finished produce, matches רבי יהודה and rejects the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: And to exclude; this tells us which opinion the rule rejects
One who exchanges or swaps; a swap counts like a sale
To cut and dry fruit into dried fruit, so its work is not yet finished
Obligated / exempt (here, in מעשר)

steps.whatToRemember: A sale fixes produce for מעשר only when its work is finished. This follows רבי יהודה against the תנא קמא of the exchange משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'to exclude' does not bring a new rule. It points to the opposing opinion that the earlier rule rejects.

phrases.english: And this excludes that which we learned in a משנה:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the first rule in step 6: a sale fixes only finished produce.

phrases.english: One who exchanges fruit with his friend,
this one to eat and that one to eat,
this one to dry and that one to dry,
phrases.notes: Literally 'to cut.' He means cutting figs and drying them, so the fruit's work isn't finished yet.

phrases.english: this one to eat and that one to dry — he is obligated.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
To eat — obligated; to dry — exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאַפּוֹקֵי מֵהָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the מקח item of רבי יוחנן's list, as steps 1 and 3 did for the courtyard and תרומה. It names the opinion that this item, which is also the first lesson in step 6, comes to reject.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rule that a sale fixes only finished produce follows רבי יהודה and rejects the תנא קמא, who says a swap always obligates.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק המביא
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the פרק המביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק המביא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line for the פרק. Nothing new is being argued here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Finishing a פרק, the learner says the הדרן to show a wish to come back and learn it again. The next line opens a brand-new פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; said when finishing a פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, "HaMeivi"

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ הַמֵּבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final discussion.

steps.title: New משנה: protecting produce from rain and leaks
steps.stepSummary: On יום טוב one may lower produce through a skylight to save it, but not on שבת. One may cover produce and jugs because of a leak, and on שבת one may put a vessel under a leak.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may lower produce through a skylight on יום טוב, but not on שבת. One may cover produce with cloths because of a leak, and the same goes for jugs of wine and jugs of oil. And one may put a vessel under a leak on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה about saving produce and other items from rain and leaks on יום טוב and שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lowering produce from the roof is hard work, so the משנה allows it only on יום טוב, not on שבת. Covering items and putting a vessel under a leak are easy actions, and the משנה allows putting a vessel under a leak even on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: One may lower or let drop down
A skylight, an opening in the roof
The leak, dripping from the ceiling
Jugs

phrases.english: One may lower produce
through a skylight on a Festival,
but not on Shabbat.
And one may cover produce with cloths
because of a leak,
and likewise jugs of wine and jugs of oil.
And one may place a vessel under a leak on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשִּׁילִין פֵּירוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֲרוּבָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lowering produce through a skylight is allowed on יום טוב but not on שבת. Covering produce and jugs because of a leak is allowed, and placing a vessel under a leak is allowed on שבת.

steps.title: Two versions of the משנה's first word
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה and רב נתן had different versions of the first word of the משנה. One said מַשִּׁילִין and the other said מַשְׁחִילִין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רב יהודה and רב נתן. One taught 'מַשִּׁילִין' and the other taught 'מַשְׁחִילִין.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by reporting a disagreement about how to say the first word of the משנה. This sets up the next lines, which will defend both versions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both words mean lowering something down, so the הלכה does not change. The question is only which word is the correct wording of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: One may let slip down; another version of the word מַשִּׁילִין

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an argument about the הלכה. Both sides agree on what you may do; they disagree only about the word.

phrases.english: Gemara: It was said:
Rav Yehuda and Rav Natan:
one taught "mashilin,"
and the other taught "mashchilin."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: רַב יְהוּדָה וְרַב נָתָן, חַד תָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Discusses the wording of the first word of the משנה in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two versions of the משנה's first word: מַשִּׁילִין and מַשְׁחִילִין.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: both readings are correct
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא rules that neither מַשִּׁילִין nor מַשְׁחִילִין is a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: Whoever reads 'מַשִּׁילִין' is not wrong, and whoever reads 'מַשְׁחִילִין' is not wrong.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא settles the disagreement from the last step by saying both versions of the word are fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה and רב נתן each had their own version of the word. מר זוטרא does not choose between them. He says both words can mean the same thing, 'to lower or drop down,' so the law of the משנה stays the same either way.

keyTerms.meaning: Whoever teaches or reads the text this way
Is not mistaken

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
One who teaches 'mashilin' is not mistaken,
and one who teaches 'mashchilin' is not mistaken.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: מַאן דְּתָנֵי ״מַשִּׁילִין״ לָא מִשְׁתַּבַּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the disagreement over the word in step 10 by accepting both versions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both מַשִּׁילִין and מַשְׁחִילִין are acceptable readings of the משנה.

steps.title: Sources for מַשִּׁילִין and מַשְׁחִילִין
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא backs up מַשִּׁילִין with a פסוק about olives dropping, and מַשְׁחִילִין with a משנה about an animal whose thigh has slipped out of place.
steps.simpleTranslation: מַשִּׁילִין is fine, because the פסוק says 'for your olives will drop off.' מַשְׁחִילִין is fine, because a משנה mentions the שָׁחוּל and the כָּסוּל. A שָׁחוּל is an animal whose thigh slipped out of its socket. A כָּסוּל is an animal with one thigh higher than the other.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא now proves that each word really can mean 'dropping down,' bringing one source for each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the root נשל means falling off, the way olives drop from a tree. In the משנה, the root שחל describes a thigh bone that slipped down out of place. Both roots carry the idea of something going down, which fits lowering produce through a skylight.

keyTerms.meaning: Will drop off or fall away
An animal whose thigh has slipped out of its socket
An animal with one thigh higher than the other

phrases.english: One who teaches 'mashilin' is not mistaken,
as it is written: 'For your olives will drop off.'
And one who teaches 'mashchilin' is not mistaken,
as we learned: The shachul and the kasul.
phrases.notes: These are two kinds of animals with damaged thighs, listed in a משנה.

phrases.english: Shachul is one whose thigh slipped out of place;
kasul is one where one of its thighs
is higher than the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּתָנֵי ״מַשִּׁילִין״ לָא מִשְׁתַּבַּשׁ, דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי יִשַּׁל זֵיתֶךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sources behind מר זוטרא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That both מַשִּׁילִין and מַשְׁחִילִין can mean 'to drop down.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'כי ישל זיתך' and the משנה about the שחול and כסול.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds three more readings
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says three more versions are also correct: מַשִּׁירִין, מַשְׁחִירִין and מַנְשִׁירִין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Whoever reads 'מַשִּׁירִין' is not wrong, whoever reads 'מַשְׁחִירִין' is not wrong, and whoever reads 'מַנְשִׁירִין' is not wrong.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא widens the list of acceptable readings with three more. His proofs come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא accepted two readings. רב נחמן בר יצחק adds three more, all close in sound and all meaning 'make fall down.' Again the law stays the same. Only the exact word changes.

keyTerms.meaning: Causing to fall off
Causing to drop down

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
One who teaches 'mashirin' is not mistaken,
and one who teaches 'mashchirin' is not mistaken,
and one who teaches 'manshirin' is not mistaken.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַאן דְּתָנֵי ״מַשִּׁירִין״ לָא מִשְׁתַּבַּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds three more acceptable readings to the two that מר זוטרא accepted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מַשִּׁירִין, מַשְׁחִירִין and מַנְשִׁירִין are also acceptable readings.

steps.title: Sources for מַשִּׁירִין and מַשְׁחִירִין
steps.stepSummary: מַשִּׁירִין is backed by the משנה that a נזיר should not wash his head with clay because it makes hair fall out. מַשְׁחִירִין is backed by the משנה calling a razor a שְׁחוֹר.
steps.simpleTranslation: מַשִּׁירִין is fine, because רבי ישמעאל says a נזיר may not scrub his head with clay, since it makes hair fall out. מַשְׁחִירִין is fine, because a משנה says a razor (שְׁחוֹר) and a barber's scissors can become טמא even when their parts are separated.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק proves his first two readings, bringing one משנה for each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מַשִּׁיר is used for clay making hair fall out, so the root means 'cause to fall.' A razor is called שְׁחוֹר because it makes hair fall, so the root שחר also carries that meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who has vowed, among other things, not to cut his hair
Scrub or wash the head
A razor
A barber's scissors
Can become ritually impure

phrases.english: One who teaches 'mashirin' is not mistaken,
as we learned: Rabbi Yishmael says:
A nazir may not scrub his head with clay,
because it makes the hair fall out.
And one who teaches 'mashchirin' is not mistaken,
as we learned: The razor and the barber's scissors,
even if their parts were separated, are susceptible to impurity.
phrases.notes: The proof is just the word שְׁחוֹר, the name of a tool that makes hair fall. The impurity law itself is not the point here.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּתָנֵי ״מַשִּׁירִין״ לָא מִשְׁתַּבַּשׁ, דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sources for the first two of רב נחמן בר יצחק's three readings.
steps.raayaObject: That the roots of מַשִּׁירִין and מַשְׁחִירִין mean 'cause to fall.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a נזיר and clay, and the משנה about the שחור and the barber's scissors.

steps.title: Sources for מַנְשִׁירִין
steps.stepSummary: מַנְשִׁירִין is backed by the משנה about clothes that fell into water, or else by the definition of לקט as what falls during reaping.
steps.simpleTranslation: מַנְשִׁירִין is fine, because a משנה says that someone whose clothes fell into water may keep walking in them without worry. Or you can prove it from the משנה: What is לקט? What falls during reaping.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק proves his third reading and offers two possible sources for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources use the root נשר to mean falling: clothes that 'fell' into water, and stalks that 'fall' during reaping. So מַנְשִׁירִין means 'cause to fall down,' which matches lowering the produce.

keyTerms.meaning: Fell down
He need not worry
Alternatively
Gleanings that must be left for the poor

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's opening word has five accepted versions: מַשִּׁילִין, מַשְׁחִילִין, מַשִּׁירִין, מַשְׁחִירִין and מַנְשִׁירִין. All of them mean 'lowering or making something fall down,' so the law is the same whichever version you read.

phrases.english: And one who teaches 'manshirin' is not mistaken,
as we learned: One whose clothes fell into water
may walk in them and need not worry.
phrases.notes: This is talking about שבת. He doesn't have to worry that people will think he washed his clothes.

phrases.english: Alternatively, from that which we learned:
What is leket? That which falls during reaping.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּתָנֵי ״מַנְשִׁירִין״ לָא מִשְׁתַּבַּשׁ, דִּתְנַן: מִי שֶׁנָּשְׁרוּ כֵּלָיו בַּמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proofs for רב נחמן בר יצחק's readings with the third one.
steps.raayaObject: That the root of מַנְשִׁירִין means 'cause to fall.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about clothes that fell into water, or the משנה defining לקט.

steps.title: How much produce may be lowered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that allows lowering produce through a skylight on יום טוב and asks what the limit is.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'We may lower produce through a skylight on יום טוב.' Up to how much?
steps.whatsHappening: After the side discussion about the exact word מַשִּׁילִין, the גמרא goes back to the rule itself and asks how much produce one may lower. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows the action but does not give an amount. Lowering produce is real effort on יום טוב, so the גמרא assumes there must be a limit and wants to know where it is.

keyTerms.meaning: A skylight, an opening in the roof
Up to how much? What is the limit?

phrases.english: We learned: We may lower produce
through a skylight on יום טוב.
Up to how much?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: מַשִּׁילִין פֵּירוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֲרוּבָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב. עַד כַּמָּה?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the word's wording and returns to the practical rule of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum amount of produce one may lower through the skylight on יום טוב.

steps.title: Four or five baskets, like the שבת case
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא in the name of רבי אסי (or רבי אסי in the name of רבי יוחנן) says the limit matches the משנה that allows clearing four or five baskets for guests or for the study hall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רבי אסי, and some say רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is like what we learned: 'We may clear away four or five baskets of straw or grain to make room for guests, or so that learning in the study hall is not stopped.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is four or five baskets. The rabbis learn this from a different משנה that sets that same amount for clearing space.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source משנה deals with moving straw and grain on שבת, and it sets a limit of four or five baskets. The answer assumes our יום טוב case works the same way, so the same number applies.

keyTerms.meaning: We may clear away, move things aside
Baskets
Learning in the study hall being stopped

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rabbi Assi,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Assi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
It is like that which we learned:
We may clear away four or five baskets
phrases.notes: This משנה is about moving things on שבת. That becomes important in the next steps.

phrases.english: of straw and of grain
because of guests,
and because of stopping the study hall.
phrases.notes: He means making room so the learning in the study hall doesn't have to stop.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּאוֹתָהּ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 by comparing it to another משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The limit is four or five baskets, the same as the משנה about clearing straw and grain.

steps.title: The שבת case had a מצוה behind it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the comparison may fail: the four or five baskets were allowed because learning in the study hall would otherwise stop, and our case has no such reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is different there, since learning in the study hall would be stopped. Here, where learning in the study hall is not stopped, it would not be allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the comparison. The other case had a special reason to allow moving the baskets, and our case does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving baskets for guests or for learning is done for the sake of a מצוה, which can justify a larger amount. Lowering produce to protect it is only for the owner's benefit, so maybe four or five baskets is too much here.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
It is different there

phrases.english: But perhaps it is different there,
since there is stopping of the study hall,
but here,
where there is no stopping of the study hall,
no.
phrases.notes: Meaning they would not allow moving that much here.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאִיכָּא בִּטּוּל בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the comparison used in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the limit from the שבת משנה, because the two cases might not be alike.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The שבת case had a מצוה reason (study hall and guests) that our case lacks.

steps.title: People might take יום טוב lightly
steps.stepSummary: A second objection: four or five baskets were allowed on שבת because people take שבת seriously. On יום טוב people might treat the day lightly, so maybe nothing at all would be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: the reason four or five baskets are allowed there is that שבת is strict in people's eyes and they will not come to treat it lightly. But יום טוב is more lenient in people's eyes, and they might come to treat it lightly, so it would not be allowed at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another reason the comparison may fail. This time the difference is between שבת and יום טוב themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since people respect שבת, allowing a little moving won't lead them to break more rules. יום טוב already feels more relaxed, so allowing any amount might lead people to treat it carelessly. So יום טוב might allow no amount at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively, or another possibility
Which is strict (taken seriously)
To treat lightly, to disrespect
Which is lenient (taken lightly)

steps.confusionAlert: Usually יום טוב is more lenient than שבת, but here that same leniency could make the rule stricter. Since people already take יום טוב lightly, the rabbis might be extra careful not to weaken it further.

phrases.english: Alternatively: there, this is the reason
that four or five baskets are permitted:
because שבת is strict
and people will not come to treat it lightly,
but יום טוב, which is lenient
and people will come to treat it lightly,
not at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: הָתָם הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא, דְּאַרְבַּע וְחָמֵשׁ קוּפּוֹת שְׁרֵי מִשּׁוּם שַׁבָּת דַּחֲמִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different reason why the comparison in step 17 might not work.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying the four or five basket limit to יום טוב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שבת is respected and safe to be lenient about, while יום טוב is taken lightly and needs extra protection.

steps.title: The other direction: money loss may allow even more
steps.stepSummary: A third objection from the opposite side: the שבת case had no money at stake, but our case involves losing money, so maybe even more than five baskets would be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, the other way around: the reason there is that there is no loss of money. But here, where there is a loss of money, even a larger amount would be allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison again, but this time it argues that our case should be more lenient, not stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the straw-and-grain case nothing is lost if the baskets stay put, so the limit stays small. With the produce on the roof, the owner stands to lose money, and the rabbis often allow more to prevent a loss. So the four or five basket limit may be too strict for our case.

keyTerms.meaning: To the other side, the opposite direction
Loss of money
A lot, a large amount

steps.whatToRemember: The answer of 'four or five baskets' was challenged from both directions. Our case might be stricter (no מצוה, and יום טוב is taken lightly) or more lenient (money is at stake). The גמרא continues with this question on the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one comparison can be attacked from both sides. A case that looks alike on the surface can differ in its reasons, and those reasons can push the law either way.

phrases.english: Alternatively, the other way around:
there, this is the reason,
that there is no loss of money,
but here, where there is loss of money,
even a lot as well.
phrases.notes: He means even more than four or five baskets would be allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי לְאִידַּךְ גִּיסָא: הָתָם הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא, דְּלֵיכָּא הֶפְסֵד מָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison of step 17 from the opposite direction of steps 18 and 19, suggesting a more lenient result.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects limiting our case to four or five baskets.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The שבת case involved no loss of money, while our case does, and that could allow a larger amount.
